strings.d1.s0.name: Grand-Place
strings.d1.s0.tips: A UNESCO square with guildhouses and the Town Hall, empty before 10:00. Manneken Pis is 2 streets away. In even-numbered years the Flower Carpet appears in August.
strings.d1.s1.name: Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert
strings.d1.s1.tips: A glass-roofed arcade from 1847, home to Neuhaus's first shop and Pierre Marcolini.
strings.d1.s2.name: Maison Dandoy Grand-Place
strings.d1.s2.tips: Speculoos and Brussels waffles (rectangular, light) since 1829. Compare with a Liège waffle (dense, sugary).
strings.d1.s3.name: Fritland
strings.d1.s3.tips: A friterie next to the square. Try the twice-fried chips and a mitraillette sandwich, part of UNESCO-recognised culture.
strings.d1.s4.name: Delirium Café
strings.d1.s4.tips: Guinness record holder with 2,000+ beers. In Impasse de la Fidélité, opposite Jeanneke Pis.
strings.d1.b0.name: Chez Léon
strings.d1.b0.tips: Moules-frites (mussels and chips) since 1893. On Rue des Bouchers.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museum of the City of Brussels Maison du Roi
strings.d1.b1.tips: The city museum in the King's House on the square, with Manneken Pis costumes.
strings.d2.s0.name: Magritte Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: 200+ surrealist works (bowler hat, apple). Combined ticket with the Royal Museums 15 EUR, closed Mondays.
strings.d2.s1.name: Place du Grand Sablon
strings.d2.s1.tips: Antique dealers and chocolatiers (Wittamer, Marcolini), plus an antiques market at weekends.
strings.d2.s2.name: Le Pain Quotidien Sablon
strings.d2.s2.tips: The chain's first branch. Try the tartines and soup.
strings.d2.s3.name: Place du Jeu de Balle Flea Market
strings.d2.s3.tips: A daily flea market in Marolles, best in the morning, in Brueghel's old neighbourhood.
strings.d2.s4.name: Musical Instruments Museum MIM
strings.d2.s4.tips: An Art Nouveau building (the Old England store). Instruments come with headphones, and the rooftop café has views.
strings.d2.b0.name: Wittamer Sablon
strings.d2.b0.tips: A pastry shop from 1910 and royal supplier.
strings.d2.b1.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts
strings.d2.b1.tips: Bruegel and Rubens. Go instead of the MIM (combined ticket with Magritte).
strings.d3.s0.name: Markt Bruges
strings.d3.s0.tips: Take the train, 1 hour from Brussels-Midi (~15 EUR). The square has the Belfry and guildhouses.
strings.d3.s1.name: Belfry of Bruges
strings.d3.s1.tips: 366 steps to the bell chamber and a panorama over the canal town. Timed tickets.
strings.d3.s2.name: Bruges Canal Boat Tour
strings.d3.s2.tips: A 30-minute boat ride past Rozenhoedkaai (the most photographed corner). 5 departure docks.
strings.d3.s3.name: De Halve Maan Brewery
strings.d3.s3.tips: Home of Brugse Zot beer. The tour takes 45 minutes plus a beer, with rooftop views. Go at lunchtime.
strings.d3.s4.name: Begijnhof Bruges
strings.d3.s4.tips: A beguine courtyard from 1245, very peaceful. Minnewater, the Lake of Love, is nearby.
strings.d3.b0.name: Frituur Bruges Markt
strings.d3.b0.tips: Two chip huts beneath the Belfry.
strings.d3.b1.name: Groeningemuseum
strings.d3.b1.tips: Flemish Primitives (van Eyck). Go instead of the Begijnhof.
strings.d4.s0.name: Atomium
strings.d4.s0.tips: The 102 m iron crystal from Expo 1958. Spheres and views, book online (combined ticket with Design Museum).
strings.d4.s1.name: Mini-Europe
strings.d4.s1.tips: 350 miniatures of Europe's landmarks, at the foot of the Atomium. Good with children.
strings.d4.s2.name: Atomium Restaurant
strings.d4.s2.tips: A restaurant with views in the top sphere. Go to the outdoor café instead.
strings.d4.s3.name: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken
strings.d4.s3.tips: Open for only 3 weeks in April and May. At other times, see Laeken Park and the Japanese Tower from outside.
strings.d4.s4.name: Parc du Cinquantenaire
strings.d4.s4.tips: A triumphal arch and museums, in the EU quarter.
strings.d4.b0.name: Frit Flagey
strings.d4.b0.tips: The city's best friterie (Place Flagey). Take the tram.
strings.d4.b1.name: Autoworld Cinquantenaire
strings.d4.b1.tips: 300 classic cars. Go instead of the park.
strings.d5.s0.name: Gravensteen
strings.d5.s0.tips: 35 minutes by train. The counts' castle has a funny audio guide and ramparts with city views.
strings.d5.s1.name: Graslei & Korenlei
strings.d5.s1.tips: Guildhouses along the canal, the best view in Ghent from St Michael's Bridge.
strings.d5.s2.name: Saint Bavo's Cathedral Ghent Altarpiece
strings.d5.s2.tips: Van Eyck's Adoration of the Mystic Lamb panel (AR tour). Opposite the Belfry.
strings.d5.s3.name: Patershol
strings.d5.s3.tips: A medieval quarter full of restaurants. Try Gentse waterzooi (chicken stew).
strings.d5.s4.name: Ghent Canal Boat Tour
strings.d5.s4.tips: 40 minutes, departing from Graslei. Then take the train back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Belfry of Ghent
strings.d5.b0.tips: A UNESCO bell tower. Go instead of the cathedral.
strings.d5.b1.name: Frituur Filip Gent
strings.d6.theme: Ixelles, Art Nouveau and the EU
strings.d6.s0.name: Horta Museum
strings.d6.s0.tips: The home of Victor Horta, the inventor of Art Nouveau, in Saint-Gilles. Timed tickets, closed Mondays.
strings.d6.s1.name: Avenue Louise Art Nouveau Walk
strings.d6.s1.tips: The façades of Hôtel Tassel and Solvay, in Ixelles.
strings.d6.s2.name: Place Flagey & Ixelles Ponds
strings.d6.s2.tips: A square and lakeside, with a market at weekends.
strings.d6.s3.name: Belga Café Flagey
strings.d6.s3.tips: A café on Place Flagey. Order a croque and a beer, opposite Frit Flagey.
strings.d6.s4.name: European Parliament Parlamentarium
strings.d6.s4.tips: A free interactive EU museum. Hemicycle tour with your passport.
strings.d6.b0.name: Moeder Lambic Fontainas
strings.d6.b0.tips: A bar for lambic and gueuze beers. A more local option than Delirium.
strings.d6.b1.name: Museum of Natural Sciences
strings.d6.b1.tips: Europe's largest dinosaur hall. Go instead of the Parlamentarium.
strings.d7.s0.name: Choco-Story Brussels
strings.d7.s0.tips: A chocolate museum with demonstrations, next to Grand-Place.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pierre Marcolini Grand Sablon
strings.d7.s1.tips: One of Belgium's best chocolatiers. Buy a gift box.
strings.d7.s2.name: Noordzee Mer du Nord
strings.d7.s2.tips: A stand-up fish bar in Sainte-Catherine. Have shrimp croquettes and white wine as a farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Gare Centrale
strings.d7.s3.tips: The train to Zaventem takes 20 minutes (Midi/Central). The bus to Charleroi takes 1 hour. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Le Pain Quotidien Sainte-Catherine
strings.d7.b1.name: Comics Art Museum
strings.d7.b1.tips: Tintin and the Smurfs, in a Horta building. Go instead of the chocolate.
strings.note0: A STIB day pass costs 8 EUR, and the city centre is walkable. Take the train to Bruges and Ghent (weekend tickets are 50% off). The train to Zaventem takes 20 minutes.
strings.note1: In December there is a light show on Grand-Place and a Christmas market (Plaisirs d'Hiver). Winter weather is 3-7°C and rainy, so museums and beer bars are warm refuges. The Laeken greenhouses open in April and May.
strings.note2: Waffles cost 3-7 EUR (Brussels = rectangular and light, Liège = dense and sugary), frites 4-6, moules-frites 25, beer 4-6. For a tip, round up the bill.
strings.note3: French is spoken in Brussels and Flemish in Bruges and Ghent; English also works. Avoid the restaurants on Rue des Bouchers (tourist traps), except Chez Léon.
strings.note4: Museums are closed on Mondays. Book Atomium and Belfry tickets online. On the first Wednesday of the month, many museums are free in the afternoon.
strings.note5: Chocolate: Neuhaus, Marcolini, Wittamer, Mary. Leonidas is cheap and good.
